status: First version (4:00 AM ET): one objective (l1_vgg) on 12 held-out images and 1 of the planned clips; the other objectives, more clips and the fine-tuned encoder are running and are added as they finish.
verdict: Partly, so far. By the numbers the encoder is a clear bottleneck: latents exist that the frozen decoder turns into much better reconstructions on every reference metric, and they lie very close to the encoder's own latents (mean change 0.06 in normalized units, where the latents have unit spread). By eye the gain is smaller than the numbers suggest: it shows as truer color, cleaner edges and fewer color fringes, not as new fine detail. The finest texture (a city seen from the air, hair strands, guitar frets) stays soft even with the best latent found, so there the decoder sets the limit. Whether a trained encoder can capture the gain is being tested now.
numbers: 12 held-out images (8 Pexels frames, 4 MAGICK on gray, 512²), latent optimized with L1 + 0.1·LPIPS-vgg for 100 Adam steps: PSNR 31.12 → 35.22 dB (+4.1 dB; every image gains, +2.0 to +6.1 dB).

Held-out judges (no objective used them): DISTS 0.061 → 0.024 (−60%), FLUX.2 latent MSE 0.329 → 0.205 (−38%), LPIPS-alex 0.055 → 0.040 (−28%); also SSIM 0.887 → 0.921, CIEDE2000 2.59 → 1.76. All 12 images improve on all six of PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS-alex, DISTS, FLUX.2 MSE and CIEDE2000.
One whole 141-frame clip (two children), 60 Adam steps through all 8 decoder chunks: PSNR 35.80 → 38.79 dB, LPIPS-alex 0.023 → 0.010, DISTS 0.043 → 0.012; flicker unchanged (0.142 vs 0.142).

Blind A/B: a fresh Sonnet agent shown 24 zoomed crops (source | A | B, order random) preferred the optimized latent in 15 of 24 (62%), mostly at its lowest confidence. My own look at the same crops agrees: truer skin and object colors and no chroma halos on graphics, but hair, frets and rooftops are about as soft as with the encoder's latent.

Sharpness (gradient and high-frequency energy relative to the source) does not rise: 0.957 → 0.941 and 0.870 → 0.843. Part of the encoder decode's 'sharpness' is grain and color fringing (MAGICK images reach 1.04–1.10 of the source), which the optimized latents remove.
The encoder's own options barely matter: the posterior mode instead of the pipeline's random sample changes PSNR by −0.2 dB on images and +0.2 dB on the clip; a tiled encode +0.45 dB on the clip.
method:
1. Samples (held out, never trained on): the 20 held-out Pexels clips of the decoder frenzy (the clips BASELINE.json scores), as whole 141-frame clips and as their frame 70 (512²), plus 8 MAGICK foregrounds over 50% gray and their Pexels backgrounds at 512² and 768².
  2. Encoder baselines: the same untiled encode as the project. Posterior sample is the latent the pipeline trains on (seeded); mode drops that noise; tiled encodes in overlapping 256² tiles.
  3. Latent optimization: Adam on the whole latent, starting at the posterior mode, learning rate 0.01 with a cosine decay to 0.001, 100 steps for images (60 for clips). The decoder is frozen and runs exactly as the pipeline decodes: bf16, 256-pixel tiles, one image decoded as its latent repeated 7 times (frame 0 kept), a clip's 8 temporal chunks together. Gradient checkpointing per decoder block; for clips the loss is taken frame batch by frame batch on a detached copy of the decode, then one backward through the decoder. Cost on one A100: about 2 s per image per step, 22 s per clip per step.
  4. Objectives: l2, l1 (pixels), lpips_vgg, lpips_alex, flux (MSE between FLUX.2-VAE latents of the decode and of the source; FIBO2's image encoder), l1_vgg = L1 + 0.1·LPIPS-vgg, l1_vgg_flux = l1_vgg + 0.01·flux, and l1_vgg with a prior that keeps the latent inside the encoder's spread.
  5. Judges: PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS (alex and vgg), DISTS (no objective uses it), FLUX.2 latent MSE, CIEDE2000, sharpness ratios, flicker (clips), all vs the source; then zoomed crops viewed by eye and a blind A/B by a fresh model agent.
  6. Fine-tuned encoder: a copy of H3's encoder trained with the decoder frozen on Bluejay train data (train Pexels clips and MAGICK images, never a held-out clip), 256² crops (one decoder tile), 34-frame windows (two encoder chunks, decoded as one 22-frame decoder chunk) plus single frames, loss L1 + 0.1·LPIPS-vgg plus a penalty on (z − zH3)² to stay in the latent distribution H3's diffusion model knows; then the same held-out scoring.
